summary: Feed s089_single to IDS is degraded due to significant packet loss (7.8% of TCP packets show missing data, threshold 1%). All other visibility checks (duplicates, encryption, VLANs, one-way, oversize, overload, truncation, tunnels) are healthy.

findings.root_cause: Upstream capture loss - 198 of 2542 TCP packets (7.79%) show sequence gaps/retransmissions indicating missing originals. Tool overload check is healthy and port is 1Gbps, so loss is not tool-side discard but upstream SPAN/mirror oversubscription or packet broker buffer exhaustion during bursts, which drops packets best-effort under load.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS needs both directions and full payload for TCP stream reassembly and signature matching. 7.8% missing segments breaks flows, prevents payload inspection, causes missed detections/false negatives and allows evasion, severely reducing detection coverage.

recommended_fix.why: SPAN/mirror ports drop packets when oversubscribed; a passive TAP with proper packet broker aggregation provides lossless, line-rate copy to the 1Gbps IDS port. If TAP already present, audit broker drops/burst buffers and add filtering to fit tool capacity.
